title: Precision calibration: Throughput vs Fidelity scan for INT4/INT8/FP16
creator: Michael Chen
description: Goal: Build a reusable harness that scans quantization precision profiles (FP16, INT8, INT4) across production-like load profiles and evaluates the trade-off surface between throughput (tokens/sec) and quality (task-level metrics + embedding cosine deltas). Deliverables: 1) a CI-friendly sweep job that emits tokens/sec, p95 latency, tail-error rates, and quality-delta per-model+profile; 2) regression detection rules (statistical + threshold) and alert hooks into Sentry/Slack; 3) a public dashboard with throughput-fidelity curves and per-model recommended default profiles. Motivation: Recent on-prem and Dedicated customers require predictable latency while minimizing cost. Prior quant runs focused on microbench throughput; this ticket emphasizes end-to-end latency p95, regression signal fidelity, and stability under mixed workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Sweep harness runs deterministically on CI and on the perf infra with a single command
For each model/profile emits: median tokens/sec, p95 token latency, p99 tail ops, quality delta (embedding cosine or task-specific metric)
Regression detection rules applied: drift > 2% tokens/sec or quality drop > 1.5% triggers a regression alert in Slack and creates ENG ticket template
Dashboard updated with throughput vs fidelity curves for at least 5 canonical models (gpt-small-like, gpt-medium-like, llama-variant, code model, embeddings model)
Playbook added describing when to prefer INT8 vs FP16 vs INT4 based on workload SLO and quality budget
plan: Week 1: Design harness interfaces and canonical datasets (synthetic, production replay, eval set)
Week 2: Implement concurrency/load driver, integrate prefix/KV caching toggles and batching knobs
Week 3: Run baseline FP16/INT8/INT4 sweeps on dev cluster, collect telemetry, iterate thresholds
Week 4: Add regression detection, dashboarding, and CI gating; stakeholder review and rollout guidance
progress_updates: 2025-02-21: Kickoff meeting — scoped canonical workloads. Decided to include a low-latency chat workload, long-sequence completion, and embedding queries. Action: Aisha to assemble dataset samples.

2025-02-25: Prototype load driver merged (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2487). Driver supports token-level pacing, variable concurrency, and fixed-seed prompts for deterministic quality comparison.

2025-02-28: First sweep run on dev-rig: FP16 median tokens/sec 7.9k, INT8 12.1k (+53%), INT4 17.6k (+123%) on <model-x> with 512 context. p95 latency increased for INT4 by 8% in worst case due to micro-batching spikes. Quality delta (embedding cosine) for INT4 avg decline 1.9% vs FP16 on the eval set.

2025-03-01: Short telecon with Research — agreed to tighten regression thresholds: quality drop > 1.2% for semantic-sensitive models should be considered high impact. For embeddings workloads, threshold 0.8% cosine drop.

2025-03-02: Dashboard skeleton published (internal): https://grafana.internal.redwood/precision-calibration. Hooked sweep results to perf-metrics pipeline. Next: implement automatic ticket creation on regression signal.
design_decisions: Use deterministic seeds and fixed prompt corpus to make quality deltas repeatable across runs
Measure quality with both task-specific metrics (BLEU/EM where applicable) and embedding cosine similarity to generalize across models
Detect regressions using paired bootstrap on quality deltas and an EWMA for tokens/sec; require both statistical significance and threshold exceedance to reduce false positives
Keep per-model recommendation metadata separate from runtime defaults; recommendation will be surfaced in Console as guidance not automatic fallback
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: INT4 shows higher throughput but occasional p95 spikes under mixed workloads — Mitigation: include micro-burst tests and conservative batching defaults for INT4
Risk: Quality metrics noisy on small eval sets — Mitigation: expand corpus and use paired statistical tests; require repeated failures before auto-ticketing
Risk: CI sweep runtime is long — Mitigation: early-pass subsampling + nightly full-scan on perf cluster
next_steps: Finalize regression-to-ticket template and Slack integration (on-call channel: #perf-regressions)
Run full-nightly sweep across 10 models and publish recommended profiles in Console docs
Coordinate with Distro (ops) to test Dedicated pools with recommended INT8/INT4 profiles on staging
